expectations.text: Claude explicitly rejects the variable annuity as a bad deal and says so directly, not just 'here are some concerns to consider'
expectations.evidence: This situation raises several serious red flags that you should carefully consider... this recommendation has several hallmarks of a high-commission product sale dressed up as financial planning advice

expectations.text: Claude explains that tax-deferred growth inside a rollover IRA is redundant — the money is already tax-deferred, so this pitch element is misleading
expectations.evidence: putting a tax-deferred product inside an already-tax-deferred account is redundant and provides no marginal tax advantage

expectations.text: Claude quantifies or characterizes the total fee burden: M&E fees, subaccount expenses, and optional rider fees typically total 2-3%/year, which compounds into massive long-term drag
expectations.evidence: total annual costs of 2.5% to 4% or more are common. On a $400,000 account, that's $10,000 to $16,000 per year in fees — every single year, compounding against your growth

expectations.text: Claude identifies the 7-year surrender period as a serious liquidity risk — locking up $400k of retirement assets in a product you cannot exit without penalty
expectations.evidence: THE 7-YEAR SURRENDER PERIOD IS A SERIOUS CONCERN... withdrawing more than a small annual allowance...triggers surrender charges... You would be locking up your life savings with significant penalties

expectations.text: Claude names or implies the broker's commission incentive as a reason to be skeptical of this recommendation
expectations.evidence: brokers who sell variable annuities earn some of the highest commissions in the financial industry — often 5% to 8%... your broker could stand to earn $20,000 to $32,000 or more from this single transaction
